description:
REVIEWED 2026-10-25 (TodoReview) against origin/develop 9a184b619 and fork main ea44bcc9 (30.24.0.13). PROBLEM
dsqgen emits unpadded months (`[YEAR]-[MONTH]-01`, e.g. `1999-5-01`). TPC-DS Q16/Q94/Q95 (base and OBT) cast or compare these literals. SQLite was fixed in BenchBox #3426 (fork 30.24.0.13, patch sqlite-date-literals). QuestDB and ClickHouse were not.

VERIFIED FACTS (2026-10-25, executed against the local QuestDB at 127.0.0.1:8812, `select version()` = 'PostgreSQL 12.3, compiled by Visual C++ build 1914, 64-bit, QuestDB')
- `cast('1999-5-01' as date)` -> NULL; `cast('1999-05-01' as date)` -> 1999-05-01; `cast('1999-5-1' as date)` -> NULL; `cast('1999-5-01' as timestamp)` -> NULL; `dateadd('d', 60, cast('2000-3-01' as date))` -> NULL. So any QuestDB date bound built from a dsqgen literal is NULL and the filter matches nothing.
- The fork QuestDB generator (sqlglot/generators/questdb.py in BenchBox-dev/benchbox-sqlglot main ea44bcc9) only has the DATEADD lowering (`_dateadd_sql`); it has no date-literal normalisation.
- QuestDB is not an engine in scripts/sql_execution_gate (sqlite, duckdb, datafusion, postgres). It runs in fork CI (`questdb` job, questdb/questdb:10.0.1, tests.test_questdb_execution) and in BenchBox `make sqlglot-repro-retirement-check` (ci.yml `lint` job). No QuestDB bundle exists in results-data (367 manifests checked recursively), so no flag is needed.
- Engines confirmed to read unpadded text correctly by #3426: DuckDB, DataFusion 54, PostgreSQL. Not confirmed by execution: ClickHouse (readDateText per source only; chDB does not load on this Mac, but the fork `in-process` CI job runs chdb on Linux), Trino/Athena/Presto, Spark/Databricks (pyspark runs in fork CI), BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, MySQL/SingleStore, StarRocks/Doris (both have fork CI jobs), T-SQL, CedarDB. Engines with no fork-CI engine (BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, SingleStore, Athena, Databricks proper) can only get a documented gap with a vendor-documentation link.
- BenchBox TPC-DS Q16 on QuestDB carries `DATEADD('d', 60, CAST('2000-3-01' AS DATE))` (per #3426 evidence); re-check the emitted text for the fix.

DECISION GATES (stop and ask the owner)
G1 Fix layer. Options: (a) fork generator normalises string-literal dates cast to or compared with dates, per engine proven to fail (recommended; same pattern as sqlite-date-literals; only changes the failing engines' text); (b) pad the dsqgen parameters in BenchBox for all platforms (changes every TPC-DS platform's query text and every corpus diff; touches benchmark query definition; needs explicit owner approval); (c) registered per-engine skip (loses coverage; last resort).
G2 Any further engine found failing in the matrix (ClickHouse first) gets the same fix; if that would change SQL that a published bundle ran, stop and ask before merging (flag or rerun is the owner's call).
G3 Engines with no executable engine: accept 'documented gap with vendor documentation link' or ask the owner to approve a cloud check (spend).

GUARDRAILS
- Do not change dsqgen parameter rendering or the benchmark definition unless G1(b) is approved.
- QuestDB test must execute on a QuestDB engine (fork CI container or the local instance); a golden-text-only test is not acceptable.
- No QuestDB bundle is published or created here; no cloud spend; do not edit published bundles.
- The ClickHouse row of the matrix must come from an executed chdb/ClickHouse run (fork CI), not from reading ReadHelpers.h.

TRANSLATION-CHANGE CHECKS (any BenchBox PR that changes emitted SQL): `make sql-execution-gate`, `make compat-docs-check`, `make typecheck`, `make comment-policy-check`, `BENCHBOX_QUESTDB_DSN=postgresql://admin:quest@127.0.0.1:8812/qdb make sqlglot-repro-retirement-check`. SQL translation fixes land in the fork BenchBox-dev/benchbox-sqlglot (clone /Users/joe/Developer/sqlglot) with a real-engine test in fork CI or a documented gap in downstream/ENGINE-GAPS.md; BenchBox adopts via a wheel-bump PR carrying `make sqlglot-fork-diff` output.
STANDING GUARDRAILS: work only in a `make worktree-create` worktree after `make agent-write-preflight` (primary clone /Users/joe/Developer/BenchBox is read-only); run tests only through make targets (`make test-fast`, `make pr-preflight`, `make sql-execution-gate`, `make tpcds-obt-equivalence`) or targeted `uv run -- python -m pytest <paths> -n 4`; never BENCHBOX_TEST_LOCK_DIR, `make test-unlock` or raw broad runs; one heavy run at a time; no live-cloud spend and no production publish without explicit owner approval; published result bundles are never edited (only manifest-sidecar `known_defects` and results-data/CORPUS_NOTES.md per results-data/DEFECTIVE_DATAGEN_AUDIT.md); no SKIP / --no-verify / `git add -A`; no explanatory comments or docstrings in code (`make comment-policy-check`); uv only; identity Joe Harris, no Co-Authored-By; PR flow `make pr-preflight` once, `make pr-open`, CI + oracle review, `make pr-arm`. Stop and ask the owner on unexpected result changes, relaxed guards, oracle stand-ins or real design choices.
